items.readable_text:
Content:
When dividing by a power of ten, we shift the digits in the place value chart to the right by the number of zeros in the power of ten.

Content:
To illustrate, let's find the value of [MATH: 47.2 \div 100.]

Content:
Step 1. Write down the place value chart for [MATH: 47.2\mathbin{:}]

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 7] | . | [MATH: 2] | | |

Content:
Step 2. Determine the number of places to move. We're dividing by [MATH: 100,] which has [MATH: \color{blue}2] zeros, so we move all values to the right by [MATH: \color{blue}2] places:

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| | | . | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 7] | [MATH: 2] |

Content:
Step 3. Put zero in all empty cells that are to the right of the decimal point. We can also put a zero in the ones place if it is empty.

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| | [MATH: 0] | . | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 7] | [MATH: 2] |

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 47.2\div 100 = 0.472 \, .]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can use place value charts to divide decimals by [MATH: 10.] For instance, to find the value of

Content:

we perform the following steps.

Content:
Step 1. Write down the place value chart for [MATH: 28]:

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths |
| [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 8] | . | |

Content:
Step 2. Move all digits by one place to the right.

Content:

Therefore, [MATH: 28\div 10 = 2.8 \, .]

Item 2 — Example: Finding Missing Values in a Place Value Chart When Dividing By Ten

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we write down the place value chart for [MATH: 12.5\mathbin{:}]

| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] | . | [MATH: 5] | |

Then, we move all digits by one place to the right.

| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths |
| | [MATH: \bbox[3pt, lightgray]{1}] | . | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: \bbox[3pt, lightgray]{5}] |

Hence, [MATH: 12.5\div 10 = 1.25\, .] The missing digits are therefore [MATH: 1] and [MATH: 5.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Dividing Decimals by Larger Powers of Ten

Content:
When dividing by a power of ten, we shift the digits in the place value chart to the right by the number of zeros in the power of ten.

Content:
To illustrate, let's find the value of [MATH: 47.2 \div 100.]

Content:
Step 1. Write down the place value chart for [MATH: 47.2\mathbin{:}]

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 7] | . | [MATH: 2] | | |

Content:
Step 2. Determine the number of places to move. We're dividing by [MATH: 100,] which has [MATH: \color{blue}2] zeros, so we move all values to the right by [MATH: \color{blue}2] places:

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| | | . | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 7] | [MATH: 2] |

Content:
Step 3. Put zero in all empty cells that are to the right of the decimal point. We can also put a zero in the ones place if it is empty.

Content:
| tens | ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| | [MATH: 0] | . | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 7] | [MATH: 2] |

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 47.2\div 100 = 0.472 \, .]

Then, we determine the number of places to move. We're dividing by [MATH: 100], which has [MATH: 2] zeros, so we move all values to the right by [MATH: 2] places:

| ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| | . | | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 3] |

Finally, we put zeros in all empty cells that are to the right of the decimal point, and also in the empty ones place:

| ones | | tenths | hundredths | thousandths |
| [MATH: 0] | . | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \bbox[3pt, lightgray]{0}] | [MATH: 3] |

Therefore, [MATH: 0.3\div 100 = 0.003 \, .] The missing digit is [MATH: 0.]
